name: fullstack
description: Skills and agents for full-stack projects (frontend + backend)

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Keep functions and components small, readable, and easy to reason about.

skills.name: design-system-reuse
skills.description: Reuse existing shared UI components and design tokens before creating new ones.

skills.name: early-returns
skills.description: Prefer early returns and guard clauses over nested conditionals.

skills.name: no-console-log
skills.description: Forbid console.log in production code; use a logger instead.

skills.name: type-safety
skills.description: Enforce strict type safety — no implicit any, no unguarded assertions.

skills.name: api-error-handling
skills.description: Use structured error responses and never leak internal details.

skills.name: llm-package-hallucination
skills.description: Verify every LLM-suggested dependency exists in the registry before installing — hallucinated package names are a real supply-chain attack surface (slopsquatting).

skills.name: lockfile-discipline
skills.description: Commit one lockfile, install from it frozen in CI and Docker (npm ci, --frozen-lockfile, --immutable), and verify npm registry signatures.

skills.name: never-read-env
skills.description: Never read .env files directly in code.

skills.name: security-secrets
skills.description: Never hardcode secrets, tokens, or credentials in source code.

skills.name: coverage-meaningful-not-vanity
skills.description: Assert observable behavior and edge cases; never write tests that execute code without asserting anything

skills.name: flaky-test-policy
skills.description: Quarantine-then-fix flaky tests; a retried test is a tracked bug, not a pass

skills.name: mocking-boundaries
skills.description: Mock at I/O and network boundaries only; never mock the unit under test; prefer fakes over deep mock chains

skills.name: test-data-builders
skills.description: Use factory or builder functions for test fixtures; never scatter inline object literals across the test suite

skills.name: test-determinism
skills.description: Avoid timing-based, random, and wall-clock assertions; use fake timers and frozen clocks instead

skills.name: test-isolation
skills.description: Each test must set up and tear down its own state; never rely on execution order or shared mutable state

skills.name: test-naming
skills.description: Name tests as "it does X when Y" — describe the behavior under a condition, not the implementation

skills.name: github-full-urls
skills.description: Link to PRs and issues with full GitHub URLs, never owner/repo#123 shorthand as the link itself (plain-prose cross-repo mentions may still use it).

skills.name: cost-accounting
skills.description: Measure LLM cost from the authoritative usage object and the provider's cost API — never from your own token estimates.

skills.name: model-selection-and-routing
skills.description: Pick models on the accuracy-vs-cost frontier and route easy queries to cheaper models — the most expensive model is rarely the right default.

skills.name: streaming
skills.description: Stream for perceived latency, but buffer tool-call JSON until the block closes and don't gate safety on partial output.

skills.name: git-move
skills.description: Use git mv for tracked files to preserve history.

skills.name: git-workflow
skills.description: Branch protection, branch naming, and PR workflow rules.

skills.name: pre-commit-checks
skills.description: Run formatter, linter, and build checks before every commit.

skills.name: chart-integrity
skills.description: One claim per chart, annotate the threshold, keep the caveat on the chart, never chart a misleading-but-true metric.

skills.name: correction-log
skills.description: Log corrections in the artifact instead of silently fixing them.

skills.name: evidence-citation
skills.description: Every number in a deliverable carries its source and its basis; own data is never dressed as research.

skills.name: measure-dont-proxy
skills.description: Never report a proxy metric when the real measurement is available; run the thing.

skills.name: no-hand-typed-figures
skills.description: Generate every figure in a deliverable from source data; never type a number in by hand.

skills.name: docs-parity
skills.description: Keep documentation in sync with every user-facing change.

skills.name: mermaid-diagrams
skills.description: Use Mermaid diagrams instead of ASCII art.

skills.name: post-edit-diagnostics
skills.description: Run diagnostics and formatter after editing code files.

skills.name: no-agent-attribution
skills.description: Never leave AI agent-attribution residue in commits, PRs, or other persisted artifacts.

skills.name: accessible-forms
skills.description: Every form control must have a programmatic label, clear error identification, and grouped fields where appropriate

skills.name: aria-only-when-needed
skills.description: ARIA is a fallback for when native HTML falls short — never add redundant or conflicting roles

skills.name: color-contrast
skills.description: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast ratios; never use color as the only visual signal

skills.name: focus-management
skills.description: Provide visible focus indicators; move focus intentionally on route change and dialog open/close

skills.name: keyboard-navigation
skills.description: All interactive elements must be reachable and operable by keyboard alone; no keyboard traps

skills.name: reduced-motion
skills.description: Honor prefers-reduced-motion; never use motion as the sole affordance for a state change

skills.name: semantic-html
skills.description: Prefer native HTML elements over div+role soup; semantic elements are accessible by default

skills.name: text-alternatives
skills.description: Provide descriptive alt text for meaningful images; empty alt for decorative; alternatives for icons and media

skills.name: workspace-hygiene
skills.description: Audits the workspace before a commit or PR — confirms diff scope, flags stray console.log/debugger/scratch files and secrets, checks atomic commits. Use after a refactor or before opening a PR.

skills.name: lighthouse-ab
skills.description: Interleaved Lighthouse A/B of two builds or URLs with the controls that keep scores comparable; reports run list, min and median. Use before claiming a change moved a Lighthouse or Web Vitals score.

skills.name: perf-attribution
skills.description: Attributes a low Lighthouse score to its cause before any fix — LCP element, pre-LCP request set, main-thread and layout-shift sources. Use when a page scores low and the cause is unclear.

skills.name: talk-deck
skills.description: Builds an evidence-backed conference deck from research data — Slidev scaffold, generated figures, demo risk triage, PDF fallback. Use when turning measured findings into a talk.

skills.name: config-echo
skills.description: Verifies bluetemberg config (rules, agents, skills) is loaded in the session by recalling from context and cross-referencing disk. Use after `bluetemberg sync` or when a rule seems ignored.

skills.name: session-retrospective
skills.description: Audits a Claude Code session — deterministic jq analysis of token spend and tool usage, then a judged retrospective in .claude/retrospectives/. Use after a task or when a session felt expensive.

skills.name: security-audit
skills.description: Triages code security findings by severity with detection steps for secrets, injection, auth, input, and dependency risks. Use when reviewing changes pre-deploy or touching auth, input, or uploads.

skills.name: pr-review-loop
skills.description: Wires automated comment-only PR reviews through a local hook that reviews PRs the moment an agent opens them. Never touches the CI/CD pipeline. Use when setting up automated PR review.

skills.name: patterns
skills.description: Finds and reuses an existing codebase pattern instead of inventing new structure. Use when adding files or abstractions, reviewing folder structure, naming, or module boundaries, or refactoring.

skills.name: orval-openapi
skills.description: Orval OpenAPI client generation: the build:api pipeline, custom fetch mutator, never hand-edit generated files, use generated hooks/types. Use when a backend API changes or editing orval.config.

skills.name: migration-safety
skills.description: Reviews or writes database schema migrations against a zero-downtime checklist — destructive ops, lock analysis, batching, rollback path. Use when creating or reviewing a migration pre-deploy.

skills.name: k6-load-testing
skills.description: Standardizes k6 load tests — scenario taxonomy, shared config/requests libs, baseline-driven p95 thresholds, __ENV parametrization, and a CI smoke gate. Use when writing or editing k6 scripts.

skills.name: integration-safety
skills.description: Safe third-party integrations: lazy init, getRequiredEnv, safeParse over parse, best-effort analytics, resilient widget scripts, hardened cookies. Use when integrating an external service.

skills.name: docs-upkeep
skills.description: Updates affected docs in the same task as code or workflow changes — README, API docs, CLI --help, config, wiki. Use when renaming endpoints, adding flags/config, or fixing stale references.

skills.name: create-skill
skills.description: Scaffold a new bluetemberg skill to the deep-skill standard — Protocol, decision trees, BAD/GOOD examples, and a completion checklist.

skills.name: create-rule
skills.description: Scaffold a new bluetemberg rule in the correct format — frontmatter, a Why/Rules/BAD-GOOD/config/gotchas body, and sync.

skills.name: create-pack
skills.description: Scaffold a whole new bluetemberg pack — package.json metadata, llm/ layout, catalog registration, and validation.

skills.name: create-agent
skills.description: Scaffold a new bluetemberg agent in the correct format — frontmatter with scoped tools, responsibilities, constraints, and sync.

skills.name: code-review
skills.description: Reviews a pull request or code diff before merge — establishes intent, reviews changed lines, reports severity-tiered findings with fixes. Use for PR review or pre-PR self-review.

skills.name: api-design
skills.description: Designs and reviews RESTful HTTP API endpoints — resource naming, pagination, error contracts, versioning. Use when creating an endpoint, reviewing an API contract, or vetting a breaking change.

agents.name: test-specialist
agents.description: Writes, refactors, and stabilizes unit/integration/e2e tests, fixes flaky/non-deterministic tests, applies fakes and data builders. Use proactively when adding tests or diagnosing flakiness.

agents.name: session-auditor
agents.description: Audits a Claude Code session transcript for token spend and harness-usage quality — wasted calls, missed delegation, cache misses — and writes a graded retrospective. Use after a session ends.

agents.name: security-specialist
agents.description: Audits code for OWASP Top 10 vulns, injection, broken auth/access control, secrets exposure, and dependency/supply-chain CVEs. MUST BE USED for deep security review. Reports findings, does not edit.

agents.name: pr-reviewer
agents.description: Headless PR reviewer — fetches PR context via gh, reviews intent-first with Conventional Comments findings, posts one comment-only review. Never approves. For in-session review use code-reviewer.

agents.name: frontend-specialist
agents.description: Implements and refactors React/Next.js UI — components, state, hooks, SSR/hydration, performance, accessibility. Use proactively when building or changing TSX/JSX UI, not for review or backend work.

agents.name: docs-maintainer
agents.description: Updates and audits documentation (README, runbooks, API docs, Mermaid diagrams) to match code, config, and workflow changes. Use proactively after behavior, CLI, API, or schema changes.

agents.name: code-reviewer
agents.description: Reviews diffs and pull requests for correctness bugs, edge cases, naming, test coverage, and maintainability. Use proactively after code changes. For deep security audits route to security-specialist.

agents.name: backend-specialist
agents.description: Builds server-side services — REST/GraphQL APIs, database access, auth flows (JWT, RBAC, OAuth/PKCE). Use proactively for API contracts, DB layers, or server auth. Not CMS schemas or security audits.

agents.name: a11y-specialist
agents.description: Audits WCAG 2.2 A/AA accessibility — semantic HTML, keyboard, focus, contrast, alt text — and reports prioritized fixes. Use proactively for UI components, forms, dialogs, screen-reader review.
